record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: For every separable infinite-dimensional Banach space X, do there exist Banach spaces Y and Z that are each isomorphic to X such that the Banach-Mazur distance d(Y,Z) equals 1 but Y and Z are not isometric?

evidence.quote: We use the following notations for Banach spaces: X ∼ Y means that X and Y are isomorphic and X ∼= Y means that X and Y are isometric.
Problem 9.1. Does for every separable infinite dimensional Banach space X there exist Banach spaces Y, Z ∈ I(X) such that d(Y, Z) = 1 and Y ̸∼= Z?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a separable infinite-dimensional Banach space. Two Banach spaces Y and Z are called isomorphic, written Y ∼ Z, if there exists a bounded linear bijection between them; they are called isometric, written Y ≅ Z, if there exists a surjective linear isometry between them. The Banach–Mazur distance between two isomorphic Banach spaces Y and Z is defined by
    d(Y, Z) = inf { ‖T‖ · ‖T⁻¹‖ : T : Y → Z is a linear isomorphism }.
Let I(X) denote the class of all Banach spaces that are isomorphic to X.

Question: Does there always exist, for every separable infinite-dimensional Banach space X, a pair of Banach spaces Y, Z ∈ I(X) such that d(Y, Z) = 1 while Y and Z are not isometric?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface related work on Banach–Mazur distance 1 phenomena (e.g., properties not invariant under distance 1, almost-isometric ideals, and the C(K) integer-distance question, which has been settled negatively), but none of the located sources state a resolution of the general question as to whether every separable infinite-dimensional Banach space admits two isomorphic copies at Banach–Mazur distance 1 that are not isometric. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: On Banach space properties that are not invariant under the Banach–Mazur distance 1
status_evidence.snippet: Studies properties P such that there exist Banach spaces with d(X,Y)=1 where X has P but Y does not — related but does not resolve the existence question for every separable space.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not settle the general existence problem.

status_evidence.title: The Banach–Mazur distance between isomorphic spaces of continuous functions is not always an integer
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves Pełczyński's question for C(K) spaces; a different question concerning Banach–Mazur distance.
status_evidence.claim: Different problem; not the one asked.

status_evidence.title: Almost isometric ideals in Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Develops the theory of almost isometric ideals; tangential to but does not settle the question.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the stated existence problem found.
